skill.name: vercel-react-best-practices
skill.description: Apply Vercel-oriented React and Next.js performance rules for data fetching, bundle size, server rendering, client fetching, re-render control, and JavaScript hot paths.
skill.summary: Audit and refactor React and Next.js code using Vercel-style performance patterns.
skill.author: ZhanlinCui

security_audit.summary: All 172 static findings were adjudicated as false positives from Markdown documentation, code examples, inline backticks, or public reference links. No prompt injection, credential handling, command execution, or unauthorized network intent was found. One medium content-trust issue remains because a community source uses official Vercel attribution that should be clarified before publication.

remediation.suggestion: Remove or qualify official maintainer wording unless affiliation is verified. State that this is a community-packaged guide and cite upstream sources clearly.

- `async-defer-await` - Move await into branches where actually used
- `async-api-routes` - Start promises early, await late in API routes
- `bundle-conditional` - Load modules only when feature is activated
- `bundle-preload` - Preload on hover/focus for perceived speed
- `server-cache-lru` - Use LRU cache for cross-request caching
- `server-serialization` - Minimize data passed to client components
- `client-swr-dedup` - Use SWR for automatic request deduplication
- `rerender-defer-reads` - Don't subscribe to state only used in callbacks
- `rerender-memo` - Extract expensive work into memoized components
- `rerender-derived-state` - Subscribe to derived booleans, not raw values
- `rerender-functional-setstate` - Use functional setState for stable callbacks
- `rerender-lazy-state-init` - Pass function to useState for expensive values
- `rendering-animate-svg-wrapper` - Animate div wrapper, not SVG element
- `rendering-hydration-no-flicker` - Use inline script for client-only data
- `js-batch-dom-css` - Group CSS changes via classes or cssText
- `js-cache-function-results` - Cache function results in module-level Map
- `js-combine-iterations` - Combine multiple filter/map into one loop
- `js-length-check-first` - Check array length before expensive comparison
- `js-min-max-loop` - Use loop for min/max instead of sort

content.value_statement: React and Next.js teams need consistent performance guidance during coding and review. This skill applies Vercel-style rules for data fetching, bundles, rendering, and re-renders.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to remove async waterfalls with Promise.all, Suspense, early promise starts, and dependency-aware fetching.
Guides bundle size reductions through direct imports, dynamic loading, and intent-based preloading.
Covers server-side React and Next.js patterns, including React.cache, LRU caching, RSC serialization, and after().
Provides client-side data guidance for SWR deduplication, passive listeners, global listener sharing, and localStorage versioning.
Documents re-render, rendering, and JavaScript hot-path optimizations with incorrect and correct examples.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples; it does not run benchmarks or measure your application automatically.
Some recommendations require Next.js App Router, React Server Components, or framework versions that support the named APIs.
It focuses on performance and does not replace security, accessibility, or product design reviews.
Static examples may need adaptation for your routing, data layer, and deployment model.

use_cases.title: Review a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Find data waterfalls, large imports, broad client props, and avoidable re-renders before code merges.

use_cases.title: Refactor a Next.js Page
use_cases.description: Convert sequential server work into parallel fetching, Suspense boundaries, and smaller client payloads.

use_cases.title: Create Team Performance Standards
use_cases.description: Turn Vercel-style rules into repeatable guidance for reviews, migrations, and feature planning.

prompt_templates.title: Find Quick Wins
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single component or page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this React or Next.js code with the vercel-react-best-practices skill. Focus on async waterfalls, bundle size, and needless re-renders. Explain each recommendation in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate refactor that should preserve behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this Next.js page using the skill. Preserve behavior while improving data fetching parallelism, Suspense boundaries, and RSC serialization. List the trade-offs you make.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Bundle Improvements
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for heavy dependencies and initial load time.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this feature for bundle size using the skill. Identify barrel imports, heavy client components, third-party libraries, and preload opportunities. Prioritize fixes by user impact.

prompt_templates.title: Run Architecture Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review across a React or Next.js workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this workflow end to end with the skill. Cover server data flow, client fetching, storage use, event listeners, rendering costs, and JavaScript hot paths. Return a prioritized remediation plan.

output_examples.input: Review a dashboard page with sequential data fetching and broad icon imports.
output: The review identifies independent requests that can start together.
It recommends direct icon imports or configured package import optimization.
It suggests Suspense boundaries for panels that do not affect the first layout.

output_examples.input: Explain why a search component renders too often.
output_examples.output: The analysis traces broad state subscriptions, unstable callbacks, and effect dependencies, then recommends narrower reads and functional state updates.

output_examples.input: Create a performance checklist for a Next.js feature launch.
output: Server work starts as early as possible and avoids sequential awaits.
Client components receive only the fields they render.
Heavy editors, analytics, and optional tools load outside the initial path.

best_practices: Start independent data work early and await results only when they are needed.
Keep client boundaries small and pass only fields that client components use.
Treat examples as patterns and measure important changes in the target application.
anti_patterns: Awaiting unrelated server work in sequence inside pages, actions, or route handlers.
Importing entire icon or component libraries through broad barrel entry points.
Memoizing everything without first narrowing state reads and effect dependencies.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps agents review and improve React and Next.js performance using structured Vercel-style guidance.

faq.question: Does it require deployment on Vercel?
faq.answer: No. Many rules apply to any React or Next.js application, although some examples reference Vercel and Next.js APIs.

faq.question: Can it replace profiling tools?
faq.answer: No. It gives review guidance and refactor patterns. You should still measure important changes with real application data.

faq.question: Which topics are covered?
faq.answer: It covers async waterfalls, bundle size, server rendering, client fetching, re-renders, rendering costs, and JavaScript loops.

faq.question: Are the examples executable by the skill?
faq.answer: No. The repository is documentation. Agents read the examples and apply the ideas to your project.

faq.question: Can teams use it for code review standards?
faq.answer: Yes. The rule files can support consistent review comments, migration plans, and performance checklists.
